description: The horizontal bar chart illustrates the number of tasks associated with various linguistic families. The vertical axis contains the categories, listing the linguistic families in descending order of their values from top to bottom without a specific axis label. The horizontal axis represents the value, labeled "# tasks," featuring a linear scale that ranges from 0 to 80 with tick marks and corresponding vertical grid lines at regular intervals of 10. Each category is represented by a single horizontal bar with a distinct color and a black outline. The longest bar at the top is for IE-Slavic, colored light blue, with a value of approximately 79 tasks. This is followed by IE-Romance (dark blue, ~47), IE-Germanic (light green, ~44), Uralic (dark green, exactly 20), IE-Baltic (light pink, ~17), IE-other (red, ~15), IE-Indic (tan, exactly 10), Semitic (dark orange, ~8), and Turkic (light purple, ~4). The shortest bar at the bottom is Basque, colored dark purple, with a value of approximately 3 tasks. The bars are sorted in strictly descending order of length, and all bars are uniformly outlined in black without any specific visual emphasis on a single category.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the distribution of tasks across various linguistic families. The vertical axis lists the categories, including IE-Slavic, IE-Romance, IE-Germanic, Uralic, IE-Baltic, IE-other, IE-Indic, Semitic, Turkic, and Basque, arranged in descending order of task count. The horizontal axis is labeled '# tasks,' ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 10. IE-Slavic exhibits the highest number of tasks, approximately 80, followed by IE-Romance at around 60 tasks. IE-Germanic and Uralic show similar task counts, both exceeding 40 tasks. Notably, IE-Baltic demonstrates a sharp decline compared to Uralic, with fewer than 15 tasks. Basque, the smallest category, has fewer than 10 tasks, showing a consistent trend of minimal representation across studies. The chart highlights a steady decrease in task counts from IE-Slavic to IE-Baltic, with a more gradual decline observed among the remaining categories.
